sections.content: A gerund attached to a subject (not necessarily opening the sentence) describes what that subject was doing at the same time as the main action — a crop rising in demand while it spread, a family growing wealthy while it exported. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: El azúcar fue el producto más importante, aumentando constantemente la demanda europea a medida que el consumo se popularizaba.
items.english: Sugar was the most important product, with European demand constantly rising as consumption became more widespread.

items.spanish: El ingenio azucarero, combinando maquinaria pesada, grandes hornos y mano de obra intensiva, funcionaba casi como una fábrica temprana.
items.english: The sugar mill, combining heavy machinery, large furnaces and intensive labor, functioned almost like an early factory.

items.spanish: Un pequeño grupo de familias acumuló fortunas cultivando y exportando cacao, convirtiéndose en una de las élites más influyentes.
items.english: A small group of families amassed fortunes growing and exporting cacao, becoming one of the most influential elites.

items.spanish: En las vegas cubanas se cultivaba un tabaco que, produciendo cosechas de gran calidad, se ganaría fama mundial.
items.english: In Cuba's small tobacco farms, a tobacco was grown that, producing high-quality harvests, would earn worldwide fame.

sections.content: A gerund placed after a comma, right next to the noun it describes (el ingenio, combinando...; un pequeño grupo de familias..., convirtiéndose...), works almost like an extra detail tucked into the sentence — remove it and the main sentence still stands on its own.
